name: Saint Aloysius Gonzaga
history: The eldest son of a marquis, trained for soldiering and the court, who gave up his inheritance to become a Jesuit. He studied in Rome under the direction of Saint Robert Bellarmine and died at twenty-three after nursing the sick in an epidemic. He is the patron of young people and of those who care for the sick.
life: Luigi Gonzaga was born at Castiglione delle Stiviere, heir to his father’s title, and was dressed as a little soldier almost as soon as he could walk. Serving at the courts of Florence, Mantua and Madrid, he saw their violence and vanity and turned to prayer. He received his first Communion from Saint Charles Borromeo. His father resisted his vocation for years, but in 1585 Aloysius signed his rights over to his brother and entered the Jesuit novitiate in Rome. He was not naturally gentle, and worked hard against his own stubbornness. In 1591 an epidemic struck Rome and the Jesuits opened a hospital. Aloysius begged in the streets for the sick and nursed them himself, and after carrying a dying man from the street he caught the disease. He died on 21 June 1591. Bellarmine, who had been his confessor, asked to be buried beside him.
prayerTo: Saint Aloysius, you gave up a title and a fortune to belong wholly to Christ, and you gave your life caring for the sick. Pray for young people, that they may be pure, brave and free. Pray for nurses and carers, and for me, that I may serve the sick as I would serve Christ. Amen.
penance: Visit, help or pray for someone who is sick, and give up some small luxury today as Aloysius gave up his inheritance.
meditation: He asked what each thing he did would matter for eternity. Ask that question once today before you choose.
prayer: O God, bestower of heavenly gifts, Who in the angelic youth Aloysius joined wondrous innocence of life to an equally wondrous love of penance; grant, by his merits and prayers, that we who have not followed him in his innocence may imitate him in his penance. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
